title: Flat quotient base change for derived coinduction with its algebra action
statement:
Let $P\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a surjective homomorphism of commutative rings, with $P$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $P\to P'$ be a flat homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Put $A'=A\otimes_P P'$. Write $C_A^P$ and $C_{A'}^{P'}$ for derived coinduction [def-trf-derived-coinduction] on ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. There is a natural transformation
$$\beta_M:C_A^P(M)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\longrightarrow C_{A'}^{P'}(M\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}P')\qquad(M\in D(P)),$$
which is an isomorphism in $D(A')$ for every $M\in D^+(P)$, where $D^+$ means cohomology vanishes in all sufficiently negative degrees. Here scalar extension is [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The transformation is characterized under the restriction--coinduction adjunction by scalar extension of the evaluation counit $\operatorname{Res}_P C_A^P(M)\to M$, $h\mapsto h(1)$, using the natural identification $\operatorname{Res}_{P'}(C_A^P(M)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A')\cong(\operatorname{Res}_P C_A^P(M))\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}P'$. Its restriction to $D(P')$ is the ordinary derived-Hom base-change map
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,M)\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}P'\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_{P'}(A',M\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}P')$$
[def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. No Noetherian hypothesis on $P'$ or bounded-above hypothesis on $M$ is imposed.

proof.text: Use the one-object category with only its identity and the topology generated by the identity cover. A sheaf of modules on it is exactly a module, so the cited sheaf constructions specialize termwise to ordinary modules. For any $A$-module $N$, the mutually inverse maps $N\otimes_A A'\to N\otimes_P P'$, $x\otimes(a\otimes s)\mapsto ax\otimes s$, and $x\otimes s\mapsto x\otimes(1\otimes s)$ are $P'$-linear and natural in $N$. The defining tensor relations verify both compositions. Thus $A'$ is flat over $A$: an injection of $A$-modules remains injective after tensoring, since its underlying $P$-linear injection does so after tensoring with $P'$. Flat tensor exactness implies that both tensor functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms (apply exactness to cycles and boundaries). Consequently their ordinary termwise functors compute derived scalar extension, and the displayed maps give the required natural identification $\theta_X:\operatorname{Res}_{P'}(X\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A')\cong(\operatorname{Res}_P X)\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}P'$ for every $X\in D(A)$. In particular $A\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}P'=A'[0]$.

source.place: The construction of equation-base-change before Tag 0E2A; flat specialization of Tag 0661 (more-algebra-lemma-base-change-comparison).

proof.text: Put $X=C_A^P(M)$ and $M'=M\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}P'$. Compose $\theta_X$ with the scalar extension of the evaluation counit $\varepsilon_M:\operatorname{Res}_P X\to M$. The restriction--coinduction adjunction for $P'\to A'$ assigns to this composite a unique arrow $\beta_M:X\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\to C_{A'}^{P'}(M')$ in $D(A')$. Naturality of the counit, of $\theta$, and of the adjunction bijection proves naturality in every $M\in D(P)$. This constructs exactly the transformation with the prescribed characterization; no boundedness assumption has been used.

source.place: Construction of equation-base-change in the section Base change for trivial duality, using Tag 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint).

proof.text: To identify the restricted arrow, represent $M$ by a K-injective $P$-complex $I$ and choose a K-injective resolution $q:I\otimes_P P'\to J$ over $P'$. The coinduction models identify its source with $\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,I)\otimes_P P'$ and its target with $\operatorname{Hom}_{P'}(A',J)$. The chain map $B(h\otimes s)(a\otimes t)=q(h(a)\otimes st)$ has these source and target. The tensor relations make it well defined; it commutes with the differential because $q$ is a chain map and $A$ is in degree zero. For $a_0\otimes u\in A'$, both $B((a_0h)\otimes us)(a\otimes t)$ and $((a_0\otimes u)B(h\otimes s))(a\otimes t)$ equal $q(h(aa_0)\otimes ust)$, so $B$ is $A'$-linear. Evaluation at $1\otimes1$ gives $q(h(1)\otimes s)$, the counit of step 2 after tensoring. Hence adjunction identifies $B$ with $\beta_M$. Forgetting the action leaves the usual derived-Hom scalar-extension map: it sends $h$ to its extended morphism, followed by $q$, and then extends $P'$-linearly. Indeed, before scalar extension the formula is $h\mapsto(a\otimes t\mapsto q(h(a)\otimes t))$; this applies the coefficient unit $i\mapsto i\otimes1$, followed by $q$, and extends each morphism to $A'$. Its $P'$-linear extension is $B$. Thus the restricted arrow is the ordinary derived-Hom base-change map for every $M$, without using an isomorphism theorem or a boundedness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0E2A (lemma-check-base-change-is-iso), identification after restriction; explicit evaluation of the map of Tag 0A6A (more-algebra-lemma-base-change-RHom).

proof.text: The $P$-module $A$ is generated by $1$, because $P\twoheadrightarrow A$ is surjective. Apply the finite-free-resolution lemma over the Noetherian ring $P$ to obtain $\cdots\to F^{-1}\to F^0\to A\to0$ with every $F^i$ finite free. In cochain degrees $i\leq0$, this is a bounded-above finite-free complex quasi-isomorphic to $A[0]$, so $A[0]$ is pseudo-coherent by definition. No finite length of the resolution is asserted.

Now let $M\in D^+(P)$. Apply pseudo-coherent derived-Hom flat base change with $R=P$, $S=P'$, $E=A[0]$, and $L=M$. Its hypotheses are exactly step 4, the assumed flatness, and the stated lower cohomological bound on $M$. The lemma specifies the map by extension of morphisms and the coefficient unit, precisely the formula checked in step 3. Since $A\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}P'=A'$, it therefore makes that restricted map an isomorphism in $D(P')$. Restriction $D(A')\to D(P')$ is conservative by the coinduction-adjunction lemma, so $\beta_M$ is an isomorphism in $D(A')$. This uses neither Noetherianity of $P'$ nor an upper bound on $M$.

The existing construction of derived scalar extension, specialized to the one-object identity-cover site, identifies the exact tensor functor with derived extension.

Uses the shared injection criterion for module flatness to prove A-prime is flat over A using the explicit tensor identity.
